Below given pie charts show the percentage population of wild animals and the percentage of land use under forest cover in different regions of the world in the year 2007.

![data set 1](/di/mod/17-s1.png)

Following are the geographical regions: A1 — Asia, China, India; A2 — Australia; A3 — Africa; A4 — Europe; A5 — Russia; A6 — North & South America; A7 — Antarctica. Population density is obtained by dividing population by land:

Population density = (Percentage Number of Animals) ÷ (Percentage Land Area Under Forest Cover).
directions: Go through the data set given below and solve the questions based on it.
question_text: If the population density of wild animals in Russia is 1, then what is the combined population density of (Africa and North & South America)?
explanation: With Russia (A5) density = 14/14 = 1, combined density of Africa (A3) and North & South America (A6) = (20+15)/(22+18) = 35/40 = 0.875 ≈ 0.88. Option (c).

question_text: A husband and wife have a combined age of 91 years. The husband is now twice as old as his wife was when he was as old as she is now. What is the difference between the husband's age and the wife's age?
explanation: Let the ages be H and W with H + W = 91. 'Husband is now twice as old as his wife was when he was as old as she is now' resolves to H = 52, W = 39. Difference = 13. Option (b).
